text.p: The governor of Buenos Aires province said that one of the airports on a list of 36 airports to be privatized may not belong to the national government, a newspaper reported Wednesday.

President Carlos Menem signed a decree to privatize the airports Monday but Gov. Eduardo Duhalde said Camet airport in the beach resort city of Mar del Plata may fall under his province's jurisdiction.
"Obviously, this has to be verified. This airport (Camet) is provincial and therefore its inclusion in a national decree may be an error," Duhalde said, according to daily El Cronista.
Duhalde added that if there were a mistake in including Camet airport, it would have to be "eliminated from the decree."
This is the latest hurdle in the airports' privatization process, which started last year.

Initially 59 airports were to be sold off but that was scaled back because the plan did not take into account the autonomy of the provinces, which have to pass laws in their local legislature before they can privatize.

The plan still includes Ezeiza international airport in Buenos Aires and the capital's domestic and short-hop Aeroparque airfield in addition to airports in the major cities of Rosario, Mendoza and the ski resort of Bariloche.
But it was uncertain whether Cordoba, Argentina's second-biggest city, would be included.

Jalil Amado, head of the civil aviation authorities in Cordoba, said his province is currently carrying out a study of the provinces' airports services which will be ready in two months, according to El Clarin.
According to Menem's privatization decree, Argentina will seek bids for a single 30-year concession to operate the airports, which will be awarded in October.
It is estimated the government could raise around $1.5 billion through the privatization.
Several international companies, including the operators of Frankfurt Airport, Aeroports de Paris and a U.S. consortium led by International Airport Group, have expressed interest.
